cards.text: Judah, one of the brothers, has just begged to stay as a slave in place of his youngest brother, Benjamin. Joseph, ruler in Egypt, has heard every word, and the brothers still don't know who he is. Now Joseph can't hold it together in front of all his attendants anymore.

cards.question: Joseph is about to break. What does he cry out to his attendants?

cards.text: Out they go. Every attendant leaves, so it's just Joseph and his brothers when he makes himself known, and then Joseph starts to weep.

cards.question: With the room cleared, Joseph weeps so quietly that nobody outside hears a thing.

cards.text: It's like stepping outside for a private phone call and then crying so loud the whole office hears. Word even reaches the household of Pharaoh, king of Egypt.

cards.question: Joseph finally says it to his brothers: "I am Joseph!" What does he ask them right after?
Joseph has just told his brothers who he is. They're so terrified in his presence that they can't answer him.

cards.text: Joseph says, "Please come near me." And they do, and I bet they do it REAL slowly.

cards.question: Up close, Joseph tells them he is Joseph, their brother, the one they ___ into Egypt.

cards.text: Now, I bet the brothers are bracing for payback. If I were them, I'd be measuring how far it is to the door.

cards.question: Joseph tells his brothers they should be distressed and angry with themselves for selling him.
Joseph says God sent him to Egypt ahead of his brothers. For what purpose?

cards.text: Then Joseph lays out the timeline. The famine has covered the land for two years now.

cards.question: Joseph says there will be ___ more years without plowing or harvesting.

cards.text: God sent him ahead, Joseph says, to preserve them as a remnant on the earth and to save their lives by a great deliverance. So it wasn't the brothers who sent him here, Joseph tells them, but God.

cards.question: Joseph says God has made him a ___ to Pharaoh, lord of all his household and ruler over all Egypt.

cards.text: Now Joseph hands his brothers a message to carry home to his father, Jacob. It starts like this: "This is what your son Joseph says: God has made me lord of all Egypt."

cards.question: Joseph's message to his father has an urgent request. What is it?

answers.text: Come down to him without delay
Stay in Canaan until the famine ends
Send more silver to buy grain

cards.question: Joseph says his father's family will settle near him in the land of ___.

cards.text: And he means everybody: Jacob, his children and grandchildren, the flocks and herds, and everything he owns. That's not "come visit," that's "bring the couch."

cards.question: Joseph says he will provide for the family in Goshen, because there will be five more years of famine.

cards.text: Then Joseph tells them that they and his brother Benjamin can see it's really him, Joseph, speaking with them. Look at the face, fellas, it's ME.

cards.question: Joseph tells the brothers what to tell his father about. What is it?

answers.text: The silver cup in the sack

cards.text: And then, again: bring my father down here quickly. I think this man has been missing his dad for a long, long time.

cards.question: Joseph throws his arms around one of his brothers and weeps. Which brother?
As Joseph and Benjamin embrace, Benjamin stays dry-eyed.

cards.text: Then Joseph kisses each of his brothers as he weeps over them. One by one, friend... that is a LONG hug line.

cards.question: Earlier, the brothers were too terrified to answer Joseph. After all the weeping, what do they do?

cards.text: Remember how word of Joseph's weeping reached Pharaoh's household? Now the news reaches Pharaoh's house that Joseph's brothers have come.

cards.question: Pharaoh and his servants are pleased that Joseph's brothers have come.

cards.text: Pharaoh gives Joseph a message for them. Load your animals, go back to Canaan, and then bring your father and your families back to him.

cards.question: Pharaoh promises to give the family the ___ of the land of Egypt.
Pharaoh has more instructions: take ___ from the land of Egypt for the young children and wives.
Pharaoh tells the brothers to be sure to pack up all their belongings.

cards.text: Forget the stuff, because the best of all the land of Egypt is theirs. That's a new job telling you, "Leave your old stapler at home. We've got you."

cards.question: Joseph hands out the wagons, provisions for the journey and new garments for each brother. But Benjamin gets more. What does he get?

answers.text: Three hundred shekels and five sets of clothes
A silver cup and two sets of clothes
A gold ring and ten sets of clothes

cards.text: For his father, Joseph sends ten donkeys loaded with the best of Egypt, plus ten female donkeys loaded with grain, bread and provisions for the trip. Twenty donkeys, friend, that's not a care package, that's a PARADE.

cards.question: As the brothers head out, Joseph tells them not to ___ on the way.

cards.text: Every group trip needs that rule, because five minutes in, somebody's arguing about the route. So the brothers go up out of Egypt and come home to their father Jacob in Canaan.

cards.question: The brothers tell Jacob that Joseph is alive and ruling all of Egypt, and Jacob believes them right away.

cards.text: Jacob is stunned. That's a whole LOT of news for one doorway.

cards.question: The brothers tell Jacob everything Joseph said. Then Jacob sees something that revives his spirit. What is it?
Jacob's spirit is revived. Then Israel, as Jacob is also called, declares, "Enough!" What does he say he'll do?

answers.text: Go to see Joseph before he dies
Send his sons back for Joseph
Wait for Joseph to come home

cards.text: "My son Joseph is still alive!" That's where we'll stop for now, friend, and trust me, this family's story is far from done.

findings.problem: This story card tells no part of the passage. It is only Papa Dorin's guess about the brothers bracing for payback, plus a joke. It cites Genesis 45:5 but uses nothing from that verse.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to guess Joseph's exact wording, 'a father to Pharaoh.' Nothing on the earlier cards lets a baker reason to 'father' over 'brother' or 'servant.' It tests wording the baker hasn't seen, not meaning they can work out.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The wrong answers 'edge' and 'corner' don't fit a pleased Pharaoh making a generous promise. They aren't believable, so 'best' stands out as the obvious pick.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: Genesis 45:21 is never told on a story card. Its content (Joseph giving the wagons and provisions) appears only as setup inside this choice question. The brothers doing as they were told is never mentioned. No card cites 45:21.

rule.text: Story card: Papa Dorin's turn. He tells the next piece of the passage. The setup for a choice is on a story card.

findings.problem: The story-continues line nearly copies the doc's example ('And that's where we'll leave it for now. Trust me, friend, this story's not done.') instead of being written fresh.

rule.text: The examples show the idea. Write your own line each time.

findings.problem: The card opens with a first-person quote, "My son Joseph is still alive!", without saying who speaks it. The speaker was named only on the previous choice card, which is no longer on screen.

rule.text: Who's speaking. When he quotes someone speaking as "I," he says who it is first.
